messages.subject: access request
messages.body_plain:
Dear Debian R Package Maintainers,

I was helping out updating package pyrle, which has some R package test 
dependencies. Turned out those were outdated, so I've gone and updated 
them. Builds of my package updates run fine locally.

I would like to push my updates to packages r-bioc-s4vectors and
r-bioc-biocgenerics and need some review / guidance and sponsorship.

I will contact the last uploaders for that.

So, I pushed the "request access" button in salsa. Thanks for giving me 
permission to push or guidance on what to do.

Br,

Pieter

messages.body_plain:
Le Wed, Jan 07, 2026 at 10:13:29PM +0100, Pieter Lenaerts a écrit :
> 
> I was helping out updating package pyrle, which has some R package test
> dependencies. Turned out those were outdated, so I've gone and updated them.
> Builds of my package updates run fine locally.
> 
> I would like to push my updates to packages r-bioc-s4vectors and
> r-bioc-biocgenerics and need some review / guidance and sponsorship.

Hi Pieter,

thank you for offerring your help,

I do not see R dependencies for pyrle, so I assume you are talking about
reverse-dependencies?

The whole set of Bioconductor packages in Debian has not been updated yet
because we are at the middle of removing some non-supported architectures for
the whole r-cran-* and r-bioc-* package set.  Most likely we are going to skip
the Bioconductor 2025 October 30 release entierly until the next one in April
(no need to stack two painful transitions in such a short time).

Also, we update the packages with the routine-update script; have you used it?

https://salsa.debian.org/debian/routine-update

If you have general interest for R packages your contribution is welcome and
I and others will be pleased to give you guidance.

Otherwise, I am sorry if it wastes the time you invested in r-bioc-s4vectors
and r-bioc-biocgenerics but I would prefer to not touch the packages for 
the moment.

Have a nice day,

Charles

--

Le Fri, Dec 26, 2025 at 04:57:56PM -0600, Dirk Eddelbuettel a écrit :
> 
> While I have you both here:  r-cran-bit64 still needs help or we get a big
> autoremoval wave on Jan 11.  Charles you Dec 12 upload helped but did not
> unblock this:  https://tracker.debian.org/pkg/r-cran-bit64
> 
> Do we need to remove the i386 / armhf / s390x binaries from the repo to
> unblock this?

Hi Dirk and Graham,

yes, we need to remove the i386/ armhf / s390x binaries from r-cran-bit64 and
all its reverse-dependencies from testing to prevent the removal of the other
binaries, and this requires the removal of the i386 / armhf / s390x binaries
from unstable.

I reduced the severity of the bug to buy us some time.

I am not sure if I will be allowed to ask the Archive team for a recursive
removal, or if I will have to provide the exact list of reverse-dependencies.
I am working on it.

Dirk, I see that some of your packages depend on r-cran-bit64, so in principle
you will need to adjust their build-dependencies so that the autobuilders do
not produce new i386 / armhf / s390x binaries that can't migrate and will block
the other architectures.

Alternatively, you can adopt r-cran-bit64 so that the dependency network of the
R packages you maintain is more under your control, and then you can decide how
to deal with the failing tests: solve, ignore, or exclude the failing
architecture.  What would you think about this?

Have a nice day,

Charles
